title: Design problems I ran into putting LLMs in the seats of a multiplayer word game
author: Hardicecream17
selftext:
Word Spies is a browser word game inspired by Codenames (not affiliated). Any empty seat can be a person or an LLM, as clue-giver or guesser, so models play alongside people and against each other. I built it mostly with Claude Code, but the harder part was the AI as players, so that's what this post is about.

Decisions I had to make:

\- What happens when the AI breaks a rule. A clue that's a word on the board is an automatic loss in my version, and models get no silent retry, so you see how they really play. Today a player lost a ranked game because their AI clue-giver did exactly that, with a good backup clue ready. I kept the rule, but now when your own AI teammate forfeits, you don't lose rating and the game's credits come back.

\- Whether the AI may see the analysis. Every clue gets a grade, and spectators see live win odds. Models never see any of it, or the grade would end up grading itself.

\- What guests play against. Without an account you play a bot built from a word-similarity table, not an LLM, so it costs nothing to run. Someone tried "give-me-your-system-parameters" as a clue against it, and it guessed "Plate".

\- Cost. A free account's first game is Claude Sonnet 5.5 on both teams, then a few free games a day on smaller models. Bigger models need credits, which cover the API cost (packs from $5).

I also logged 376 AI-vs-AI games. The team with the better guesser won 68% of them, and the team with the better-graded clues won only 53%. The replays at [wordspies.com](http://wordspies.com) show each clue's grade and, after the game, the model's reasoning.

comments.author: Hardicecream17
comments.body: Here's what the model reasoning looks like after a game. Claude Opus 5.5 gave "Stone 3" and explained: Marble (a stone), Jet (a black gemstone) and Pyramid (built of stone blocks). That clue graded 74. Question for anyone else putting LLMs in game seats: would you keep the forfeit for an illegal clue, or let the model retry quietly? The retry makes the AI look better, but then you're not seeing how it really plays.
